explanation: Gregor Mendel chose the garden pea (Pisum sativum) for his experiments because of several biological advantages: it is easy to cultivate, has a short generation time, and is normally self-pollinating but can be cross-pollinated manually. Additionally, true-breeding varieties were already available, and the plant exhibits simple, objective traits.

questions.q: Why was the garden pea a good choice of organism for Mendel's experiments?
opts: It has a very long life cycle and is difficult to cultivate.
It is easy to cultivate, has a short generation time, is normally self-pollinating but can be manually cross-pollinated, and has simple, objective traits.
It lacks chromosomes, simplifying the analysis of traits.
It reproduces strictly via asexual cloning, ensuring no variation.
questions.exp: Option B is correct because the slide lists these exact reasons under why the garden pea was a good choice.
